newsitem.title: HONG KONG: British artist bids for world helicopter record.
newsitem.headline: British artist bids for world helicopter record.

text.p: British artist Jennifer Murray, bidding to be the first woman to fly a helicopter around the world, dropped into her Hong Kong home on Tuesday to join the handover-to-China celebrations.

Swoooping low over Kai Tak airport to land amid the jumbo jets that roar in across the rooftops of Kowloon, she was greeted with a hug and kiss by Britain's last colonial governor, Chris Patten, at the halfway point in her epic voyage.
Murray and co-pilot Quentin Smith have clocked up 19 countries so far, ducking sandstorms in Saudi Arabia and just missing a massive thunderstorm that hit Hong Kong harbour.
"I cannot believe I am home. To be in Hong Kong in our little helicopter is really stunning," said the 56-year-old grandmother elegantly attired in a designer flying suit.
The pair, bidding to fly around the world in 97 days, hit rough weather over the English Channel when starting on May 10 but Murray said: "Since then, the gods have been smiling on us."
They even had time en route to stop over for the Monaco Grand Prix and enjoy a quick peek at Mount Everest.
Patten, performing one of his last functions before handing Hong Kong back to China on June 30, said: "This is a good, old-fashioned adventure carried off with great dash and courage.
"When Leonardo Da Vinci first dreamed up the helicopter, I don't think he had anything like this in mind. You certainly deserve more than a Mona Lisa smile after this."
The pair, who hope to raise 500,000 pounds for The Save The Children Fund, leave on July 2 once China has taken over the colony.
Murray, carrrying a four-leaf clover given to her by her mother, said: "We have had amazing good fortune with the weather. I think the gods are looking after us so far."

"We just avoided a sandstorm in Saudi Arabia and were able to fly above one in India," she said. Their only problem was a three-day delay in Dubai waiting for a worn bearing to be replaced. "Everyone is dying for a bit of drama," she said.

The duo, flying in their R44 piston helicopter, head next to Japan and on to the remote wildernesses of eastern Russia before crossing the Bering Straits. In New York they are to land on the USS Intrepid before the gruelling last leg back to England over the glaciers of Greenland and Iceland.
